concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: standalone art-direction concept for Turris Damnatorum, a third-person gothic action roguelite. A plausible in-game 3D view, not an asset pack or character illustration.
Input image: the supplied screenshot is a reference for the game's subject, gameplay camera and arena layout, NOT for its existing rendering style.
Scene: a knight seen from behind at lower center-left, full body, sword in right hand, shield on left arm, facing one angular winged demon in the mid-distance. Broad walkable stone arena with a circular sigil, repeating gothic wall sections, a few intact and broken columns, hanging banners and torches. Keep open readable combat space. Same basic scene and medium-wide over-the-shoulder gameplay framing across concepts; hero occupies about one quarter of image height. Wide landscape composition.
Production constraint: visually beautiful using achievable economical 3D assets: simple clean silhouettes, modular repeated architecture, limited material families, deliberately restrained surface detail. The style itself must do the visual work. Do not rely on photorealistic scans, ornate sculpted filigree, dense props, microdetail, or cinematic depth of field. Clear enemies and navigation, restrained stylized VFX. Rigid armored boots, convincing anatomy.
No HUD, no text, no labels, no watermark. One coherent scene filling the entire image; no collage or swatches.
STYLE 1 — GOTHIC ANIME: a confident three-dimensional anime game render with crisp two- or three-band cel shading and selective thin dark contours. Mature elongated but simplified knight silhouette, large planar ivory armor plates over deep navy cloth, a single crimson waistcloth, no tiny buckles or ornate etching. Walls and columns made from large pale stone shapes, angular graphic shadows, a few architectural voids framing a deep blue evening sky. Cool blue shadows and warm amber torch accents. Demon is charcoal with a small red-orange core and a strong legible silhouette. Sparse sweeping stylized magic strokes. Graphic clarity and deliberate shape design; polished animation-film art direction translated into feasible low-to-medium-poly 3D, not painterly illustration. Mood: solemn and heroic, ominous without muddy darkness.

STYLE 2 — HAND-PAINTED TABLETOP DIORAMA: visibly three-dimensional chunky hand-painted miniature aesthetic, grown-up dark fantasy with tactile painted wood-and-stone feel. Compact robust knight with thick armor and oversized readable sword and shield; beveled broad armor planes, simple separate armor shells. Muted teal armor, ochre-brown leather, short burgundy fabric. Low polygon-count moss-green and warm gray stone arena, large repeating block modules with rounded worn edges, a restrained handful of broad hand-painted strokes and edge highlights, no high-frequency grime. Warm amber torches, cool green ambient shadows, atmosphere like a beautifully lit miniature set. A stout angular dark demon painted violet-black with pale horns. Camera remains full-scale third-person gameplay, NOT an isometric view or photographed model on a table. Show how broad form, a small texture palette, and lighting make economical models feel rich. Not cute chibi, not photorealistic, no tilt-shift blur.

STYLE 3 — LIVING WOODCUT / DARK GRAPHIC NOVEL: a feasible 3D scene presented as a striking medieval linocut print. Bone-ivory stone, large ink-black shadow masses, muted parchment sky, with small vermilion accents only on banners, hero cloth and demon magic. Sharply readable low-poly geometry. Flat shading with sparse directional hatching confined to shadow transitions and selective ink contours, NOT thousands of engraved details. Knight is a bold angular armored silhouette, faceless enclosed helm, plain slab-like sword and shield; demon has an exaggerated iconic horned/winged silhouette. Giant simple arches and repeated squared buttresses replace ornate cathedral detail. Subtle paper grain unifies the image. Mature uncanny ritual atmosphere with dramatic negative space. It must still read as navigable third-person 3D gameplay, with clear ground planes, depth and a fair visible enemy, rather than a flat poster or drawing pasted over a screenshot.

STYLE 4 — JEWEL-TONE FACETED LOW-POLY FANTASY: exceptionally clean simplified polygonal 3D with beautiful bold color relationships. No black ink outlines, no cel-shaded anime bands, no painterly textures. A faceted midnight-purple fortress arena floats visually in a soft dusty lavender twilight; tall simple split monoliths and pointed arches, large orderly floor stones with an understated geometric gold sigil. A few turquoise magical flames and warm peach-gold side lighting; atmospheric layers give depth. Knight has a powerful slightly exaggerated silhouette, broad untextured dark plum steel armor with pale silver bevels, a small orange cloak, oversized readable blade; demon is a few angular charcoal forms with restrained coral emissive cracks. Beauty comes from silhouette, flat color materials, low-poly bevel highlights and composition. Modular architecture with very few reusable shapes, no tiny rubble carpets or ornamental sculpture. Dark fantasy rather than neon science fiction, ominous but colorful, elegant and practical for a small game's asset pipeline.
